entries.value: "The graph's RECORD STORE, as a database (epic-retire-json-ledgers-for-db-and-git-drivers). One row per record, queried by id; every version ever written kept as rows and appended by TRIGGER, so no write path can skip recording history and a bad write is recoverable by moving back a version. Replaces the 27.5 MB committed JSON ledger, the 50 MB runtime blob, and the four-copy propagation between them."

lead: # The shared SQLite helpers every store in this workspace opens through (plandb/skilldb/logs/json-store),
# so the graph store resolves its path, migrates and reads exactly as its siblings do rather than
# inventing a fourth way to open a database.
# The same rusqlite every SQLite store here links (plandb/skilldb/compliance): `bundled` so the store
# does not depend on a system SQLite, matching its siblings rather than introducing a second answer.
# `vendored::sha256_hex` — the ONE content-hash form in this workspace, for the ledger's signature.
# `preserve_order` — LOAD-BEARING, and not merely inherited. This crate's promise is that exporting
# `main` reproduces the store it imported, BYTE for byte; a BTreeMap sorts every record's keys on the
# way through and rewrites all 1,808 files to no effect. It was passing only by cargo's per-invocation
# feature unification with `bsc-graph`, which sets it — so `cargo test -p bsc-graph-store` silently got
# a BTreeMap and the export guard could not see key-order drift at all.
# build.rs parses the committed graph store directly — see crates/graph-materialize/build.rs.
# THE SHARED CRATE ROOT — this crate owns no source file at all. See
# crates/graph-materialize/crate_root.rs; the crate's own docs come from its record.
